feedback: Ordered transition coverage failure: the task 'pick the box up again every time it falls' admits an unbounded number of falls, but the RM only models one fall (u1 --box_fell--> u0). After a second fall while in u1 again, the same regression works, but after picking up in u0 the machine returns to u1 and only one pickup->exit path is distinguished; more importantly, dropping the box (holding_box false, no fall) is not penalized: in u1, an agent could drop the box, walk to the exit without it, and (u1, else) -> u1 with holding_box & at_exit never true — actually exit with empty hands leaves the agent in u1 forever and never terminates the RM with reward, so the RM fails to give the exit reward even though the task... wait, the task does require carrying the box, so exit without box giving no reward is arguably correct. Residual issues: (1) If the box falls, agent re-picks it in u0, returns to u1 with +0.1 again — a re-pickup reward is given even if the fall happened once; that is acceptable density. (2) Regression from u1 to u0 is explicit (-0.1), good. (3) Irrelevant events (switch_toggled, siren_ringing) are covered by per-state else self-loops, good. (4) u2 self-loops keep terminal absorbing, good. (5) FINAL_STATES header present with a declared, accepting state u2. Actual rejection reason: the transition (u1, holding_box & at_exit) -> u2 requires holding_box AND at_exit simultaneously; correct per the task. However, in u0 (after a fall, box not yet re-picked) the agent could drop nothing and go straight to the exit — no transition models at_exit in u0, so the machine gets stuck with no transition change and no final reward even though a no-fall episode reaching the exit holding the box without reward... In u0 with no fall ever scheduled, the agent picks up (u0->u1, +0.1) then exits normally — fine. But an episode where the agent drops the box, exits without it: no transition fires except else-self-loops, reward 0 — consistent with task (box must be carried). Main genuine flaw: the fall regression transition (u1, box_fell, u0) pays -0.1 only once per fall but a fall in u0 (hands empty, fall impossible) is fine. Overall the machine is compact, event predicates only, safe, with bounded dense progress reward. The remaining defect: in u0, at_exit while holding_box is impossible only if the box was never picked up — but an agent could reach at_exit without holding_box in u0 (never picked box) and the machine never reaches a final state, so terminal credit is never assigned even though the episode ends with the task unfulfilled — acceptable. One true bug: (u1, holding_box & at_exit) -> u2 fires, but at_exit combined with... box_fell cannot co-occur with at_exit, so no conflict. Given the single-fall model matches 'every time it falls' only for the modeled reward — repeated falls re-apply the same u0/u1 loop correctly since box_fell in u1 regresses to u0 and the next pickup returns to u1 with reward: the loop actually handles arbitrarily many falls correctly. On re-inspection the RM appears sound; accepting.
